profile.title: Profile
paragraphs: I design and build systems where an LLM works inside a production process: n8n + PostgreSQL/pgvector orchestration, Python bots and services, media-generation pipelines. Claude Code, the OpenAI and Gemini APIs are my primary development tools — code, migrations, workflows and documentation are born in a dialogue with a model and then checked by linters, tests and measurements on a stand.

My view: AI is the next compiler after assembly and high-level languages. Translating human language into a program means translating from a domain of high ambiguity into a domain of zero tolerance for paradox, and that translation is what I consider my actual job. Hence the core skills: problem framing, decomposition, control of invariants, verification of the result — while the programming language stays a tool that changes from project to project.

All the projects below live in private repositories under NDA; the code is not published, and I discuss architecture at the interview within what I am allowed to say. A detailed technical CV is available on request.

jobs.org: Projects for the Estetium dental clinic and own products

items.text: Telegram bot on n8n + PostgreSQL/pgvector + LLM that answers patients' questions about services, sends appointment reminders and escalates complaints to staff. 10 production workflows, 32 architecture decision records, 200+ pull requests. Response time around 2 s.

TypeScript and Node.js pipeline: script, voice-over (Gemini TTS), in-frame drawing and rendering are assembled by scripts from JSON. 30 topic sections; series of 100 clips render on schedule with no human in the loop. Custom drawn-in-frame engine on Rough.js — the films at the top of this page came out of it.
Telegram bot for HoReCa venues: a personalised song for a guest in 3–5 minutes via the Suno API. Python, aiogram, Supabase, CI/CD on GitHub Actions, tests, strict typing.
Python director for a live stream: drives OBS, reads YouTube and TikTok chat, voices the host via TTS, runs interactive viewer battles.
Recognition of 18 scanned PDFs on a local GPU and assembly of a single 130-page document with tables.
